headline: They put on life vests. Then the boat rolled. All 197 lived.
summary: A tanker that had lost its steering hit the American Heritage, a river cruise boat docked in New Orleans, on Friday. The crew put life vests on everyone before it rolled. All 197 passengers and crew survived; 32 went to hospital, none critical. The port has sued the tanker's owner, and a judge handed the ship to federal investigators.

cover_question.q: Why put life vests on first?

cover_answer: The boat was leaning. When it rolled, people floated.
table_question: Which safety rule do you follow even when it feels pointless?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: On Friday in New Orleans a big tanker ship couldn't steer and bumped into a riverboat tied up at the dock. The crew got everyone into life vests, and when the boat rolled onto its side, like a toy boat tipping in the bath, the vests kept everyone's heads up until tugboats and police pulled them out. All 197 people got out. Nobody is missing.
5-7.why: The toy boat tipping is the one picture. Vests on, heads up, everyone out is the order that calms.
5-7.why_long: A seven-year-old takes one picture, a boat on its side, for the whole event, and reads your face before your words. So the script puts the toy boat in the bath next to the life vests and ends on everyone out. Expect "could our boat tip over?" You are not on a boat. This one was hit, and everyone had a vest on.

8-12.script: The tanker's steering failed, so it drifted like a shopping cart with a jammed wheel into the American Heritage at its dock. The crew put life vests on everyone before the boat rolled; the harbor police chief says that saved lives. All 197 people survived. Now the port is suing the tanker's owner.
8-12.why: A chain they can follow: no steering, hit, vests, roll, out. The jammed wheel is why.
8-12.why_long: At nine the chain is the thing: no steering, the ship kept going, it hit the docked boat, vests went on, the boat rolled, everyone floated. The jammed wheel is the mechanism, and the vests are the rule that worked before anyone knew it was needed. Expect "why did the steering break?" Nobody knows yet. Investigators have the ship.

13-17.script: Who pays when a ship loses its steering? The port sued within hours and investigators hold the tanker. Second: the crew put life vests on everyone before the boat rolled; the harbor police chief credits that for zero deaths. Which rules do you keep before you need them?
13-17.why: A lawsuit and a rescue in one story: two true things. Let them pick the thread.
13-17.why_long: A fifteen-year-old can hold two true things: a port suing within hours, and a crew whose one call, vests on first, is what the harbor police chief credits for zero deaths. The script hands them both and asks which rules they keep before they need them. Expect "was it the tanker's fault?" The steering failed. Why is still unknown.

5-7.a: Yes. All 197 people. Thirty-two went to hospital and none of them is badly hurt.

8-12.q: Why put life vests on first?
8-12.a: The boat was leaning. It rolled, and about 100 people floated.
The port sued the tanker's owner. Investigators hold the ship.

13-17.a: The port claims $1 million in damage and wanted the ship held.
AP says a Chinese state firm's subsidiary. It didn't answer AP.
